subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Hindsight Bias
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Hindsight Bias.

hook.text: After the 2008 crash, everyone claimed they saw it coming. Before the crash, almost nobody acted on it.

buildup.text: Hindsight bias rewrites memory. Once you know the outcome, your brain inserts it into the past as obvious.

discovery.text: Fischhoff proved this in 1975: people given outcomes rated them as predictable even when they were random.

twist.text: This bias blocks learning. If every outcome feels obvious, you never update how you make decisions.

climax.text: Record your predictions before events happen. Comparing forecasts to outcomes reveals your real accuracy.

punchline.text: If you knew it all along, prove it. Show the receipt.

quiz.question: Why does hindsight bias block learning?
options: It makes failures seem too painful to revisit
It makes outcomes feel obvious so you never improve your process
It erases all memory of the event
